governing_question: Even if a policy is fiscally possible and legally allowed, how will real households, businesses, workers, investors, landlords, consumers, local governments, and markets actually react to it?
stance: Economics changes when humans respond. No proposition may rely on people behaving better than ordinary people actually behave.

ordinary_humans_lock.statement: The system must function with ordinary human beings pursuing varied goals, making imperfect decisions, and responding to incentives.
ordinary_humans_lock.note: Locked as Stage 4 behavioral standard if architecture remains. Not a moral-superiority theory of citizenship.

behavioral_failure_modes.plain: Someone takes more risk because another party bears losses.
behavioral_failure_modes.label: MORAL HAZARD

behavioral_failure_modes.plain: A program disproportionately attracts costly/high-risk participants.
behavioral_failure_modes.label: ADVERSE SELECTION

behavioral_failure_modes.plain: A third party absorbs intended household benefit.
behavioral_failure_modes.label: BENEFIT CAPTURE

behavioral_failure_modes.plain: Actors use political rules to gain economic advantage.
behavioral_failure_modes.label: RENT SEEKING

behavioral_failure_modes.plain: People technically comply while defeating policy purpose.
behavioral_failure_modes.label: GAMING

behavioral_failure_modes.plain: Small income changes cause large benefit losses.
behavioral_failure_modes.label: CLIFF EFFECTS

behavioral_failure_modes.plain: Public action replaces rather than supplements private activity.
behavioral_failure_modes.label: CROWD OUT
LOCK-IN
behavioral_failure_modes.plain: A program creates dependency or makes switching expensive.
Efficiency lowers cost and increases usage enough to offset expected savings.
behavioral_failure_modes.label: REBOUND EFFECT

household_benefit_capture_test.title: Household Benefit Capture Test
household_benefit_capture_test.chain: policy change → business/government response → prices/wages/taxes/access → household resources/costs/security/ownership/time
questions: Can another party raise prices because the household now has more resources?
Is the effect temporary or durable?
household_benefit_capture_test.finding: Any intervention that stops at legal payer or first recipient is incomplete. Benefit capture is the default red-team presumption until supply response and pricing power are checked.

tax_incidence.title: Tax incidence — legal payer ≠ economic payer
tax_incidence.rule: Attack every major revenue type by tracing burden through prices, wages, returns, rents, employment, and investment.

types.likely_burden: Consumers; more regressive for necessities with inelastic demand
Split among prices, wages, and capital returns — context-dependent
Owners short run; can capitalize into prices/rents; tenants via rent; buyers via purchase price
Users; may be more progressive if optional, regressive if essentials
Must be mapped per feeder; COUNTABLE still $0 so incidence of hoped-for cash is speculative

tax_incidence.safeguard: Every revenue proposition must publish a legal-payer vs economic-burden note. Fake precision forbidden where elasticity unknown.

housing.title: Housing — biggest behavioral trap
housing.core: If household income/subsidy rises and supply does not, purchasing power becomes higher bids → higher prices/rents.
housing.finding: Subsidy-without-supply is FAILED BEHAVIORALLY as a household-prosperity strategy. Zoning/supply expansion + ownership reforms are SURVIVED ONLY UNDER CONDITIONS. OV-32-06 / OV-36-03: capitalize-into-rents is the default risk unless supply responds.
housing.hostile: Demand-side relief with inelastic housing supply is a landlord/landowner transfer machine dressed as household aid.

healthcare.title: Healthcare household response
attacks: If household exposure falls, utilization may rise
Provider prices may respond
Capacity may not expand
Rural providers may still fail
Insurance may shift costs elsewhere
Demand may outrun workforce supply
healthcare.punch: Greater access without greater capacity can produce queues rather than care.
healthcare.safeguard: Access claims must be paired with capacity/workforce constraints — route deep design stress to 4.4 resilience.

education.title: Education / residency incentives
attacks: Subsidized resident demand may exceed capacity
Institutions may capture subsidy via tuition/fees
Students may choose weak-value programs
Demand Map may become political workforce planning
Strategic recruits may not stay
Graduates may leave after subsidy
Service-linked support may distort careers
Residency rules encourage strategic domicile claims
education.legal_note: 4.2: bona fide differentials OK; durational traps constrained. 4.3: incentives and gaming.
education.finding: Heavy subsidy without capacity + stay/value tests is HIGH GAMING RISK. Service-reciprocal design SURVIVED WITH BEHAVIORAL SAFEGUARD (voluntary, non-coercive, portable where possible). CTE pathways UNPROVEN quantitatively (OV-33-05).

labor.title: Work and labor incentives
attacks: Benefit cliffs reduce net household prosperity from work
Employer benefits create job lock-in
Worker ownership may concentrate household risk if wages + retirement ride the same firm
Workers may prefer cash to equity
AI transition may raise productivity without household surplus
labor.punch: Worker ownership can increase wealth AND concentrate household risk. Diversified claims may be safer than employer-concentrated equity.
labor.safeguard: Any worker-ownership push must disclose concentration risk and allow cash alternatives.

entrepreneurship.title: Entrepreneurship response
attacks: New capital may fund marginal businesses chasing same local demand
Failure rates, collateral, insurance, healthcare dependency constrain entry
Not everybody should become an entrepreneur
entrepreneurship.punch: The system must remain prosperous for people who choose ordinary employment.
entrepreneurship.finding: Capital-access-as-universal-entrepreneurship FAILED BEHAVIORALLY as a slogan. Targeted capability + market-size realism SURVIVES UNDER CONDITIONS.

public_capital.title: Public Capital Additionality Test
public_capital.question: Did public participation cause productive activity that would otherwise not occur, or did it merely subsidize something the market would have done anyway?
risks: Projects structured to maximize public participation
public_capital.finding: Public equity/participation without additionality test is HIGH GAMING RISK / FAILED BEHAVIORALLY as default. Additionality + waterfall + no private debt guarantee (4.2) are required safeguards.

procurement.title: Procurement behavioral response
procurement.legal_note: 4.2 killed blanket Arkansas-first; lawful toolkit remains.
tradeoffs: Preference margins may raise public prices
OR help new local firms achieve scale and long-run competition
procurement.finding: Short-run cost vs long-run competition tradeoff must be explicit. Preference without entry/graduation metrics is HIGH GAMING RISK.

retention.title: Local retention and consumer behavior
attacks: Would households pay 1% / 10% / 30% more for local?
Quality differences matter
Low-income households may not afford buy-Arkansas premiums
retention.punch: Productive retention must not become a moral burden on households who need affordable goods.
retention.finding: Confirms 4.1 counterfactual test. Retention-as-virtue-signal FAILED BEHAVIORALLY.

credit.title: Banking and credit behavior
attacks: Easier credit → asset price inflation
Weaker underwriting → defaults
Risk shifted to government
Overleverage
Politically favored sectors get cheap capital
credit.punch: Access to credit is not automatically access to prosperity. Sometimes more credit simply means more debt.
credit.finding: Public bank not required by architecture. Existing authorities/CDFIs/ring-fenced funds preferred; cheap-credit expansion without underwriting discipline FAILED BEHAVIORALLY.

external_investment.title: External investment — Capability Transfer Test
external_investment.question: When does external capital build Arkansas capability, and when does Arkansas become merely the location of someone else's productive asset?
external_investment.finding: Out-of-state ownership is not binary bad. Capability Transfer Test required. Extraction-without-transfer is MARKET OFFSET / capture risk → 4.5.

migration.title: Migration / population response
attacks: Prosperity raises housing demand and land values
Displacement risk for existing residents
Public-service demand rises
Population growth ≠ prosperity; decline ≠ failure if per-household capability rises
migration.safeguard: Population strategy needs a capacity constraint (housing, schools, water, healthcare workforce).

pilots.title: Pilot Transferability Test
pilots.punch: Pilot success does not automatically imply scale success.
questions: What conditions made the pilot succeed?
What happens in the weakest county?

fiscal_visibility.title: Fiscal Visibility
fiscal_visibility.finding: Public-income can create an illusion that government resources are free and weaken fiscal discipline. Citizens must see opportunity cost of public assets, resources, and retained earnings. 'Government didn't tax us' ≠ free money.

elasticity.title: Elasticity as validation risk marker
elasticity.rule: Every major economic model must identify where it assumes behavior will not change. Those assumptions are validation risks. Full elasticity estimates not required this pass.

market_structure.title: Market-structure test
questions: Does this increase or decrease viable competitors?
Lower or raise barriers to entry?
Move concentration upstream/downstream rather than remove it?

effects.note: Renters may see temporary relief then rent capture; owners capitalize.
Capitalization and landlord pass-through uncertain; not automatic tenant win.
Moral premium hits constrained budgets hardest.
Taxpayers fund; institutional capture and out-migration risk.
Wealth upside + concentration risk if firm fails.
Can raise assets or debt burden; defaults asymmetric.

five_scenarios_rule.title: Five scenario families
five_scenarios_rule.rule: Any mechanism that only works in INTENDED RESPONSE is fragile.

proposition_board.proposition: Ordinary-humans lock — system must work without morally superior citizens
Household Benefit Capture Test as required gate
Demand-side housing relief without supply response helps households durably
Housing supply expansion + ownership reforms
proposition_board.note: OV-36-03 modeling still open; wealth effects mixed

proposition_board.proposition: Access expansion without capacity expansion = more care
Heavy resident education subsidy without stay/value/capacity tests
Voluntary service-reciprocal benefits (non-coercive)
Worker ownership always improves household prosperity
Worker ownership with cash alternative + risk disclosure
More entrepreneurship capital always raises prosperity
proposition_board.note: Marginal firms / ordinary employment must remain viable

proposition_board.proposition: Public capital without additionality test
Public Capital Additionality Test + waterfall
Lawful local procurement preferences without graduation metrics
Buy-local moral premium as household duty
Easier credit = prosperity
proposition_board.note: May mean more debt / asset inflation

proposition_board.proposition: Public bank required for capital access
proposition_board.note: OV-34-05 — architecture does not require; prefer existing tools

proposition_board.proposition: Capability Transfer Test for external capital
Population growth = prosperity
Pilot success implies statewide success
proposition_board.note: Selection bias — Pilot Transferability Test required

proposition_board.proposition: Fiscal Visibility for public-income systems
Legal payer = economic payer
CTE / multiple pathways improve household surplus vs credential-only
proposition_board.note: OV-33-05 — directionally plausible; Arkansas evidence incomplete

ov_cx_disposition.note: Discretionary time measurement — no fake precision; method still open (joins OV-32-05)
County Prosperity Surplus microsim not published this pass; behavioral gates defined first
Energy burden by quintile/county still needs primary bind
Childcare prices/slots/cliffs — cliffs flagged as failure mode; numbers unbound
Wealth / medical debt / emergency savings distribution still open
Same family as OV-31-05 — refuse fake annual precision
Housing-cost relief capitalizes into rents without supply/ownership reforms — FAILED BEHAVIORALLY as default
CTE vs credential-only household effects — plausible; not cleared
Service-reciprocal must be voluntary/non-coercive; gaming and career distortion flagged
Housing supply vs existing wealth modeling still open; absorption risk established
Human transition costs must book into Household Prosperity Ledger — method open, requirement locked
Public bank not required; existing authorities + CDFIs + ring-fenced funds preferred; credit≠prosperity

what_changed_format.what_we_expected: Fiscally possible and legally allowed policies would transmit benefits to households if designed with good intentions.
what_changed_format.how_people_markets_could_react: Benefit capture, capitalization into rents, institutional subsidy capture, moral hazard around public capital, gaming of residency/procurement, weak entrepreneurship response, credit-as-debt, pilot selection bias, fiscal illusion.
what_changed_format.what_evidence_supports: Standard incidence/housing capitalization logic; public-choice and moral-hazard literature patterns; Pass 4.1 retention counterfactual; Pass 4.2 legal narrowing of preferences.
what_changed_format.what_breaks: Demand-side housing without supply; access without capacity; worker-ownership-as-always-good; credit-as-prosperity; buy-local moral premiums; pilot→statewide leap; public capital without additionality.
what_changed_format.what_needs_guardrails: Benefit Capture Test; incidence notes; Additionality Test; Capability Transfer Test; Pilot Transferability Test; Fiscal Visibility; five-scenario fragility rule; cash alternatives to concentrated equity.
what_changed_format.what_remains_unknown: County microsim; energy burden binds; childcare cliffs numbers; wealth/debt distribution; CTE surplus evidence; full elasticity tables.
what_changed_format.what_we_changed: Locked ordinary-humans standard; killed several slogans behaviorally; required tests before claims of household transmission.

architectural_changes.detail: No proposition may require morally superior citizens.
Alongside waterfall and no private debt guarantees.
